key_insight: HPO stabilizes sparse-reward RL by down-weighting negative-advantage updates and using mean-length normalization, with A-HPO automatically adapting that balance from batch statistics.
engineering_relevance: It offers a minimal drop-in change to GRPO-style training that can improve early-stage learning efficiency without requiring a separate fixed hysteretic hyperparameter.
method: Reduce the update weight for negative-advantage responses to avoid destabilizing early sparse-reward training.
Replace per-response length normalization with mean-length normalization to decouple update scale from output length.
Use adaptive hysteresis (A-HPO) to set the negative-update weight from batch-level advantage-sign statistics.
evidence_signal: In TeleLogs and Countdown experiments, A-HPO improved reward per update, reaching 0.84 final reward on TeleLogs and showing the largest gains in early, difficult sparse-reward settings across 1.5B–7B models.
watch_item: Results come from sparse-verifiable-reward benchmarks, so the gains may depend on the reward sparsity pattern and on careful implementation of the hysteretic weighting and normalization scheme.
paper_title: HPO: Hysteretic Policy Optimization for Stable and Efficient Training under Sparse-Reward Regime
